test: host-access: e2e/specs/state-color.spec.ts > @host-access a per-request rule wears the running spine, not the at-rest grey
reason: Replaced by "every rule tone paints its own spine on both row surfaces". The former assertion encoded the defect; the replacement verifies every declared tone, including doubt, on both row surfaces and their direction glyphs.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/badge.spec.ts > engages the Chrome-managed count badge
reason: Replaced. The count badge is gone from the product: planBadge in src/core/badge.ts paints the active profile's badge text, with pause as the only override, and no source references displayActionCountAsBadgeText. The same shipped project covers what took its place, in the same file: "paints the active profile's badge text and colour" and "repaints the badge when the active profile changes".

test: shipped: e2e/specs/badge.spec.ts > paints the needs-access Chrome badge amber
reason: Replaced. planBadge has no amber state left to assert; needs-access is per site, so it moved onto the rows that can name the site. The shipped project still covers the browser-visible half through grants.spec.ts "the site-access page mirrors the browser's granted and needed origins". The popup row state is not paintable on any e2e build, for the reason set out above that test, and is covered by src/test/popup.test.tsx and src/ui/state/readout.test.ts.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/conflicts.spec.ts > overlapping header operations follow visible priority order
reason: Replaced. This test launched a browser and never used it: it called compileDynamic and findOverriddenRules directly. Its priority-order half is asserted by src/core/compile.test.ts ("applies higher priorities first, admits only later appends, stops after remove, and separates request from response"); its shadowing half by src/ui/state/project.test.ts, which covers the successor to the deleted src/core/conflicts.ts; and the browser-observable half by conflicts.spec.ts "Chrome applies set/append/remove conflicts in visible order" under host-access.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/conflicts.spec.ts > reordering changes the set operation that takes effect
reason: Replaced. Also compile-only, with no browser interaction. Rule order deciding priority is asserted over generated arrangements in src/core/compile.test.ts, shadowing after a reorder by src/ui/state/project.test.ts, and which operation actually reaches the wire by conflicts.spec.ts "Chrome applies set/append/remove conflicts in visible order" under host-access.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/grants.spec.ts > a target-and-initiator rule is a silent no-op while access is missing
reason: Replaced in the same shipped project, in the same file, by "an enabled rule with no grant is compiled out of the ruleset entirely". It keeps the on-the-wire check that the header never appears and strengthens the rest: the installed ruleset is asserted empty rather than merely unchanged.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/header-matrix.spec.ts > header operations reconcile into accepted browser rules
reason: Moved to host-access under the same name. It reads back the rule Chrome accepted, and the shipped artifact holds no host grant, so the background compiles the rule away and nothing is installed to read. grants.spec.ts asserts that emptiness in shipped, so this test cannot run there.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/lifecycle.spec.ts > reconcile repairs direct dynamic-rule corruption and converges
reason: Moved to host-access under the same name. Repair is observed by comparing installed rules against the compile, and an ungranted rule compiles to nothing in shipped, so there is no installed rule to corrupt or to repair.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/lifecycle.spec.ts > seeded rule reconciles into DNR and reads back normalized-equal
reason: Moved to host-access under the same name. The normalized read-back it asserts only exists on a build that holds the grant; in shipped the fixture would wait for a rule the background never installs.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/popup-header.spec.ts > the popup options button opens the options workspace
reason: Replaced in the same shipped project, in the same file, by "the popup options button opens the About page". It still asserts the button opens options.html on the extension origin, and additionally pins the route the button now targets.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/this-tab.spec.ts > a navigation with no visible url drains the override and it stays ended across a round trip
reason: Replaced by "a cross-origin navigation drains the override and it stays ended across a round trip" under host-access. Same drain-and-stay-drained property, now asserted on a real cross-origin hop: the shipped version could only see it because that build hides tab.url, so every navigation pruned. host-access also gains "a same-site navigation and an SPA route change keep the override", the distinction the shipped version could not make.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/this-tab.spec.ts > a This-tab override compiles to a session rule confined to its tab and origin
reason: Moved to host-access under the same name. emitRules keeps an ungranted This-tab row out of the session band, so there is no compiled condition left in shipped to inspect. The shipped project keeps the complementary guarantee as "the shipped build keeps an ungranted This-tab row out of the session band".

test: shipped: e2e/specs/this-tab.spec.ts > closing a tab ends its overrides
reason: Moved to host-access under the same name. It waits for the session rule to be installed before closing the tab, and emitRules only puts one in the session band when the build holds the grant.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/this-tab.spec.ts > cross-tab confinement holds regardless of open same-origin and cross-origin tabs
reason: Moved to host-access under the same name. With no grant the session band stays empty, so shipped has no installed rule whose tabIds could show the confinement this asserts.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/dnr-contract.spec.ts > matches Chrome's dynamic-rule boundary
reason: Moved to host-access under the same name. It relies on seedStateAndWait, whose precondition is the host-access build's all-sites grant (measured: an unconfined seedState here races the background's own reconciliation of the seeded doc, which can strip a probe rule that landed while it was still computing its removal batch).

test: shipped: e2e/specs/dnr-contract.spec.ts > rejects an invalid batch atomically
reason: Moved to host-access under the same name, for the same reconciliation race as the sibling test above.

test: narrow-host-access: e2e/specs/layout-invariants.spec.ts > this-tab composer names the narrowed grant it will ask for
reason: Replaced in the same narrow-host-access project, in the same file, by "this-tab composer offers Add without a grant when a narrowed grant covers the tab's origin". The and-allow label is no longer reachable on any e2e build because origin-level coverage means any grant that makes the tab URL readable also covers its origin. The label is pinned by src/test/this-tab-popup.test.tsx and src/ui/copy.test.ts.

test: shipped: e2e/specs/popup-header.spec.ts > the popup options button opens the About page
reason: Replaced in the same shipped project, in the same file, by "the popup options button opens the options workspace". The button is labelled Options and now opens the options page where the browser opens it, so the assertion moved from the About route to the page's own default section; the replacement still pins the extension origin and path, and additionally pins that About keeps its own nav entry there.
